children: The S&P Global Hong Kong SAR PMI declined to 49.2 in September 2026 from 49.1 in August, marking the second straight month of contraction.

It was the fastest contraction in private-sector business activity since April, as new orders and output fell for the second consecutive month due to challenges in the economic environment, including a decline in customer numbers and competitive pressures.
Foreign sales rose for the first time in three months and at the sharpest pace since May.
Employment continued to decline, with the sharpest fall in almost six-and-a-half years.
Meanwhile, purchasing activity increased, helping inventory levels to rise for the fifteenth time in the past 16 months.
Delivery times lengthened due to higher transportation costs.
On the price front, input costs rose, boosted by higher raw material costs, while output cost inflation eased due to discounts as part of efforts to boost sales.

title: Hong Kong Private Sector Contracts the Most in 5 Months
